dedupe_keys.name: co2 transport planning database v3 0 netl edx 60 weighted geospatial layers on legislation land use existing infrastructure and hazards for co2 pipeline routing in the u s

description: The CO2 Transport Planning Database of the National Energy Technology Laboratory gathers the geospatial layers needed to route carbon dioxide pipelines across the United States. The Energy Data eXchange page, read on 2026-09-28, describes version 3.0 as more than 70 GB of data on state legislation, land use requirements, existing infrastructure and hazard prevention areas, in which more than 60 layers carry a weight from zero, for more acceptable areas, to one, for areas to avoid, set from current legislation and pipeline construction recommendations; the database is the baseline of NETL's Smart CO2 Transport Planning Tool. It is offered as a zipped shapefile set, a file geodatabase, a readme and a metadata spreadsheet. The 2023 data article on version 1 lists 47 source datasets grouped into protected areas, public and energy infrastructure, environmental justice factors, potential risks, regulations and natural features. Coverage is the contiguous United States, with some layers for Alaska and Hawaii. The data are free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the weights are planning judgements, not measured costs, and the layer list of version 3.0 was not read. It supports pipeline route optimisation and exposure studies, such as least-cost routing of a CO2 trunk line around seismic, flood and protected areas. No related CO2 pipeline planning record is catalogued.
